cites.quote: closed by staff once its start time has passed
An appointment that is booked and still open.
Blood group, allergies, chronic conditions, current medications and notes of one patient.
An appointment called off before it took place, with a reason
then it returns the same patients as before this change, each row with a Last visit value
A paged query that joins appointments naively could repeat patient rows

findings.suggested_fix: Make the Given include a matching patient with two Completed appointments plus a Cancelled and a No-show. Make the Then say each matching patient appears in exactly one row.
findings.text: S-3 AC2 only says search returns the same patients. A naive appointment join could repeat a matching patient's row and still return the same set of patients, so the AC would pass. The intent flags this risk.

cites.quote: where the 1st and the 20th each have several Completed, Cancelled and No-show appointments
the 1st and the 20th patient each have two Completed appointments plus a Cancelled and a No-show appointment

findings.suggested_fix: Change the body summary to match the front-matter counts.
findings.text: The body summary of S-3 AC1 says 'several' appointments. The front-matter criterion says exactly two Completed plus one Cancelled and one No-show.

cites.quote: then none of the medical history values appear in the list, including in the Last visit column
No medical history appears in the patient list.

findings.suggested_fix: If the data-protection rule covers list responses, add that the data behind the list also contains no medical history fields.
findings.text: S-5 AC1 only checks what is visible in the list. It would not catch medical history sent in the list's data but not displayed. REQ-13 only says it must not appear in the patient list.

questions.text: Does 'No medical history appears in the patient list' (REQ-13) also cover the data the list receives from the server, or only what is shown on screen?

rubric_items.reason: All 15 known REQs (REQ-1 to REQ-15) are traced: S-1 covers 1-6 and 14, S-2 covers 7-8, S-3 covers 9-11 and 15, S-4 covers 12, S-5 covers 13. The intent has no assumed REQs.
Each story is mostly one outcome. S-1 also carries REQ-14 (no highlight or filter). S-3 bundles three regressions: paging, search and sort.

The ACs are Given/When/Then and mostly discriminating: a time-zone case where the local and UTC dates differ, latest start vs latest closed, each excluded status, and paging with duplicate risk. The search AC would not catch duplicate rows.

Asia/Kolkata and 20 per page come from the intent. UTC+05:30 is derived inline from Asia/Kolkata. 21 patients follows from 20 per page plus one row on page two. The dates and times are test data, not limits.
Terms are clear and consistent with the glossary. The body summary of S-3 AC1 differs slightly from the front-matter criterion.
